questions.question: If all truck drivers and transport operators across India decide to go on a nationwide strike, what immediate economic consequence will follow?
options: The agricultural sector will automatically double its food grain output
Farmers will be unable to sell their vegetables and milk, causing produce to rot, while urban factories shut down due to lack of raw materials
Software companies will begin manufacturing heavy diesel trucks
Wholesale commodity prices in urban retail markets will drop to zero
questions.explanation: This demonstrates sectoral interdependence: the tertiary sector (transport) links primary agricultural producers to urban consumers and secondary factory processors. Without transport, both primary and secondary sectors collapse.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Economics, Chapter 2, Section 2.1 (Table on Interdependence)

questions.question: A farmer cultivates raw cotton (Primary), a textile mill spins yarn and weaves cloth (Secondary), and a wholesale trader transports and markets the shirts to retail stores (Tertiary). This value chain proves that:
options: Raw cotton can be converted into shirts without any industrial processing
Wholesale traders belong exclusively to the primary agricultural sector
Secondary manufacturing can operate without raw materials from nature
Economic sectors do not function in isolation; each successive sector adds economic value to the output of preceding sectors
questions.explanation: Each stage in the supply chain builds upon the preceding stage: primary provides raw natural fibre, secondary transforms it into fabric and garments, and tertiary distributes it to the consumer.

questions.question: Does disguised unemployment exist only in rural agriculture, or is it also visible in urban areas?
options: It is also visible in urban areas among thousands of casual street vendors, cart pushers, and repair persons who spend the whole day working but earn very little
It is strictly illegal and non-existent in urban municipalities
It only affects software engineers working in multinational corporate firms

questions.explanation: There are thousands of casual workers in the service sector in urban areas who search for daily employment (painters, plumbers, repair persons, street vendors). They may spend the whole day but earn very little; they do this work because they lack better opportunities.

questions.question: Over the past forty years, industrial production in India grew by more than 9 times while industrial employment grew by only around 3 times. Similarly, service output grew by 14 times while service employment grew by only 5 times. What fundamental structural challenge does this reveal?
options: Indian workers refuse to accept employment in factories or offices
The Indian economy has completely de-industrialized since 1970
Growth in secondary and tertiary sectors has been capital-intensive, failing to generate sufficient employment commensurate with output growth ('jobless growth')
The primary sector has completely absorbed all surplus urban engineers
questions.explanation: While production in service and industry expanded dramatically, employment did not grow at the same pace. As a result, more than half the country's workers remain stuck in primary agriculture where output per worker is low.

questions.question: If India were to ensure that all children aged 5 to 17 attend quality schools as envisioned under the Right to Education, what significant employment outcome would emerge?

questions.subtopic: Credit as a Catalyst for Rural Employment
questions.question: Why is the provision of cheap and affordable formal credit to small farmers considered a vital strategy for employment generation?
options: It allows farmers to permanently stop farming and move to luxury resorts
It forces commercial banks to forgive all corporate urban debts
It allows farmers to purchase seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation equipment without falling into the debt-trap of exploitative local moneylenders
It eliminates the need for agricultural harvests
questions.explanation: Small farmers need credit for seeds, fertilizers, pumps, and pesticides. If local commercial or cooperative banks provide credit at reasonable interest, farmers can invest, grow multiple crops, and generate sustained on-farm employment.

questions.question: Is the entire service sector in India expanding and prospering uniformly?

No; only highly skilled services (IT, software, finance) are booming, while millions of unorganized service workers (hawkers, domestic maids, auto drivers) earn barely enough for survival

questions.question: In India, what critical social reality intersects with employment in the unorganised sector?
options: A vast majority of workers in unorganised jobs belong to Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and backward communities, facing both economic insecurity and social discrimination
Unorganised workers belong exclusively to upper-caste royal dynasties
Caste has zero correlation with unorganised labour representation
Scheduled Castes are constitutionally barred from working in the unorganised sector
questions.explanation: A majority of workers from scheduled castes, tribes and backward communities find themselves in the unorganised sector. Besides getting the irregular and low-paid work, these workers also face social discrimination. Protection and support to the unorganised sector workers is thus necessary for both economic and social development.

questions.question: A farmer sells wheat to a flour mill for ₹10 per kg. The mill grinds the wheat and sells flour to a biscuit company for ₹12 per kg. The biscuit company uses flour, sugar, and oil to produce 4 packets of biscuits and sells them to consumers at ₹20 per packet (Total ₹80). What is the total value added to GDP?
options: ₹10 (only the primary agricultural wheat)
₹22 (₹10 wheat + ₹12 flour)
₹80 (the final market value of the biscuits)
questions.explanation: In GDP, only the value of final goods and services is counted. The biscuits are the final good reaching the consumer, valued at ₹80. All intermediate values (wheat ₹10, flour ₹12) are already embedded in the final ₹80 price.

questions.question: How does India's sectoral transition differ fundamentally from the classical path followed by advanced industrialized nations like Britain and the USA?
options: India industrialized completely before developing any primary agricultural sector
India has never developed any service or transport infrastructure
India has 90% of its workforce employed in heavy steel foundries
India leapfrogged directly from an agrarian economy to a service-dominant GDP economy without the manufacturing sector ever becoming the principal employer of labour
questions.explanation: Unlike Western economies where surplus agrarian workers shifted first to factory manufacturing, India's secondary sector generated relatively few jobs; the GDP shift bypassed secondary dominance straight into services, leaving surplus labour stranded in agriculture.
